plan_details.specific_competence: Care for garments and maintain cleanliness.
plan_details.main_activity: a) Washing  garments  following  steps of  washing  them.
plan_details.teaching_learning_resources: basin, water soap clothes, brooms, timetables, water soapbananas meat heat source recipes, tea milk blender flourpens books musical instruments theater traditional music instruments
plan_details.references: TIE(2019)Vocational Studies For Primary Schools Pupils Book, Standard Six. Dar es salaam

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: - Discuss the importance of washing clothes for hygiene and appearance. <br> - Show different types of garments and discuss if they all need to be washed the same way.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: - Understand why washing clothes is important. <br> - Observe different garments and think about how they are usually washed. <br> - Identify the basic stages of washing.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Garments have been properly washed following the steps of washing them.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: - Demonstrate how to sort clothes (by color and fabric type). <br> - Explain the difference between hand washing and machine washing (if applicable). <br> -
teaching_structure.learning_activities: - Learn how to sort clothes correctly. <br> - Understand the difference between hand and machine washing. <br> - Observe the hand washing demonstration.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Garments have been properly washed following the steps of washing them.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: - Provide students with different small fabric samples. <br> - Ask them to sort the samples as if they were going to wash them. <br>
teaching_structure.learning_activities: - Sort the fabric samples according to color and type. <br> - Create a step-by-step guide for hand washing a chosen garment.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Garments have been properly washed following the steps of washing them.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Use portfolios, performance assessment, and questions and answers
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Students present portfolio, answer questions orally and perform tasks
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Garments have been properly washed following the steps of washing them.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: - Discuss why we iron clothes (remove wrinkles, look neat). <br> - Introduce the basic ironing equipment (iron, ironing board). <br> - Emphasize safety precautions when using an iron (hot surface, electricity).
teaching_structure.learning_activities: - Understand the purpose of ironing. <br> - Identify the basic ironing tools. <br> - Recognize the safety rules for using an iron.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Clothes have been ironed properly following the required procedures.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: - Demonstrate how to set up the ironing board safely. <br> - Demonstrate basic ironing techniques on a simple garment (e.g., a handkerchief or small towel), showing different strokes and heat settings
teaching_structure.learning_activities: - Observe the safe setup of the ironing board. <br> - Watch the ironing demonstration carefully.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Clothes have been ironed properly following the required procedures.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: - Provide students with clean, slightly wrinkled fabric squares. <br> - Under strict supervision and with safety guidance, allow students to practice ironing their fabric squares.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Practice ironing their fabric squares under close supervision. <br> - Observe the difference before and after ironing. <br> - Share their experience and learning points.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Clothes have been ironed properly following the required procedures.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Prepare physical model, use interviews and short quizzes
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Present prepared model, attempt quizzes and participate in interview
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Clothes have been ironed properly following the required procedures.

teaching_structure.learning_activities: - Understand who a "customer" is. <br> - Recognize why understanding customers is important. <br> - Share their experiences with different types of customers.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Types of customers have been identified correctly according to the products available.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: - Guide students to identify different types of customers based on their behavior and needs (e.g., loyal customers, new customers, demanding customers)
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Learn to identify different customer types. <br> - Discuss strategies for interacting with various customers.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Types of customers have been identified correctly according to the products available.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: - Present scenarios involving different customer types. <br> - Ask students to role-play how they would interact with each customer in a business setting.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: - Role-play interactions with different customer types. <br> - Discuss the importance of providing good customer service.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Types of customers have been identified correctly according to the products available.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Prepare physical model, use interviews and short quizzes
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Present prepared model, attempt quizzes and participate in interview
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Types of customers have been identified correctly according to the products available.

plan_details.main_activity: Identify  cheating  that can  be done  by people  who share a  business.
plan_details.teaching_learning_resources: basin, water soap clothes, brooms, timetables, water soapbananas meat heat source recipes, tea milk blender flourpens books musical instruments theater traditional music instruments
plan_details.references: TIE(2019)Vocational Studies For Primary Schools Pupils Book, Standard Six. Dar es salaam

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: - Introduce the concept of "ethics" in business (doing what is right and fair). <br> - Discuss the importance of honesty and fairness in business dealings.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: - Understand the meaning of "ethics" in business. <br> - Recognize the importance of honesty and fairness. <br> - Identify basic examples of unethical practices.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Cheating in a shared business has been identified.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: - Discuss various unethical business practices, such as: <br> - Selling faulty goods <br> - Misleading advertising <br> - Treating customers unfairly
teaching_structure.learning_activities: - Learn about specific unethical business practices. <br> - Understand the negative consequences of these practices
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Cheating in a shared business has been identified.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Present scenarios involving ethical dilemmas in business. <br> - Ask students to discuss what the right thing to do would be in each situation and why. <br> - Encourage critical thinking and moral reasoning.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: - Analyze ethical dilemmas in business scenarios. <br> - Discuss and justify ethical courses of action.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Cheating in a shared business has been identified.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Employ use of flashcards, questions and answers and written assignments
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Respond to flash cards answer oral questions and written assignments
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Cheating in a shared business has been identified.

plan_details.main_activity: Specify  valid  devices used  to measure  various  products.
plan_details.specific_activity: Devices for Measuring Products for Sale
plan_details.teaching_learning_resources: basin, water soap clothes, brooms, timetables, water soapbananas meat heat source recipes, tea milk blender flourpens books musical instruments theater traditional music instruments
plan_details.references: TIE(2019)Vocational Studies For Primary Schools Pupils Book, Standard Six. Dar es salaam

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Discuss the importance of accurate measurement when selling products. Introduce different devices used for measuring products for sale (e.g., scales, measuring cups, rulers).
teaching_structure.learning_activities: - Understand why accurate measurement is important in selling.  Identify various measuring devices.  - Learn the uses of different measuring devices.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Valid measuring devices used to measure various products have been specified correctly.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: - Demonstrate how to use each measuring device correctly. <br> - Emphasize the importance of using calibrated and accurate devices.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: - Observe the correct use of each measuring device. <br> - Understand the importance of accurate and calibrated devices. <br> - Discuss the impact of inaccurate measurements
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Valid measuring devices used to measure various products have been specified correctly.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: - Set up a mock "market" in the classroom with different products for "sale."  Provide students with measuring devices and ask them to "sell" the products, ensuring accurate measurements.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: - Participate in the mock market activity.  "Sell" products using accurate measurements.  Practice using measuring devices correctly.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Valid measuring devices used to measure various products have been specified correctly.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Use portfolios, performance assessment, and questions and answers
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Students present portfolio, answer questions orally and perform tasks
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Valid measuring devices used to measure various products have been specified correctly.

plan_details.specific_competence: Know the principles of money management.
plan_details.main_activity: Identifying  the types  of registers  that are  used to keep  records of  goods and  money.
plan_details.specific_activity: Keeping Records of Goods and Money
plan_details.teaching_learning_resources: basin, water soap clothes, brooms, timetables, water soapbananas meat heat source recipes, tea milk blender flourpens books musical instruments theater traditional music instruments
plan_details.references: TIE(2019)Vocational Studies For Primary Schools Pupils Book, Standard Six. Dar es salaam

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: - Discuss the importance of keeping records in a business (knowing what you have and how much money you have).  - Introduce simple methods for keeping records: Inventory (list of goods)
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Understand why keeping records is important in business.  - Learn about inventory and cash books.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Registers for recording goods and money have been identified correctly.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: - Demonstrate how to create a simple inventory list (listing items and quantities). Demonstrate how to create a basic cash book (recording income and expenses). Work through examples with the class.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: - Learn how to create an inventory list. <br> - Learn how to create a basic cash book. - Practice creating these records.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Registers for recording goods and money have been identified correctly.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: - Provide students with a scenario involving a small business (e.g., a school supply store).  Ask them to create an inventory list and a cash book for the business, based on the given information.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: - Create an inventory list and cash book for a given business scenario.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Registers for recording goods and money have been identified correctly.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Employ use of flashcards, questions and answers and written assignments
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Respond to flash cards answer oral questions and written assignments
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Registers for recording goods and money have been identified correctly.

plan_details.specific_competence: Know the principles of money management.
plan_details.main_activity: Identifying  the four  types of  taxes that  are paid for  sold goods.
plan_details.specific_activity: Four Types of Taxes Paid for Goods Sold
plan_details.teaching_learning_resources: basin, water soap clothes, brooms, timetables, water soapbananas meat heat source recipes, tea milk blender flourpens books musical instruments theater traditional music instruments
plan_details.references: TIE(2019)Vocational Studies For Primary Schools Pupils Book, Standard Six. Dar es salaam

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: - Introduce the concept of "taxes" as money paid to the government.  Explain that taxes help fund public services.  Discuss the idea that taxes are often included in the price of goods.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: - Understand what "taxes" are.  Recognize that taxes help pay for public services.  Learn that taxes are often part of the price of items.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: The required four types of taxes that have to be paid are identified correctly.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Introduce four common types of taxes related to goods sold (adapt to your specific Kenyan context, but examples include):  Excise Duty Import Duty (if applicable)  Sales Tax (if applicable)  Explain what each tax is and how it is applied.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: - Learn about four types of taxes related to goods sold.  Understand the purpose and application of each tax.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: The required four types of taxes that have to be paid are identified correctly.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Provide students with examples of receipts or price tags for various goods. - Ask them to identify which taxes might be included in the price and explain their reasoning
teaching_structure.learning_activities: - Analyze receipts or price tags to identify potential taxes. <br> - Discuss the role of taxes in the economy.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: The required four types of taxes that have to be paid are identified correctly.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Use portfolios, performance assessment, and questions and answers
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Students present portfolio, answer questions orally and perform tasks
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: The required four types of taxes that have to be paid are identified correctly.
